You are a Python repair worker on a personal executive-assistant repository at /mnt/d_drive/repos/EA. Your current working directory is a scratch task directory; use it only for ./notes.md. Make your code change in the repository at that absolute path.

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY, enforced by the check. You own exactly ONE repository file: scripts/sources/intake.py. Do not modify, create, delete, reformat or stage anything else. In particular: tests/test_gmail_partial.py is FROZEN and hash-checked -- if you edit it the check fails immediately and your work is discarded. Do not touch anything under _config/, do not touch AGENTS.md or ROUTER.md, do not touch ~/.claude/skills/, do not run git commit, git push, or git add -A, and do not create __pycache__ outside the repo's existing ignore rules.

DO NOT call any network API, do not retrieve any secret, and do not run scripts/sources/intake.py against live sources. Everything you need is provable offline against the frozen test.

THE BUG. In a scheduled run on 2026-08-07, the source `gmail-mybcat` died because ONE message returned HttpError 400 from `messages().get`. In `gmail_items` (around line 84 of scripts/sources/intake.py) the per-message `get` has no exception handling, so that single failure escaped the loop and destroyed the entire source: 100 messages of inbox picture lost to one bad id. The daily brief built on that scan then reported meeting RSVPs as missing when they had in fact arrived and were sitting in the inbox the scan had silently dropped. Reporting an unfinished search as a finding is the single worst failure this repository is built to prevent.

THE CONTRACT you must implement, ruled by the project's design authority:

  attempted = the number of messages the adapter tried to fetch
  errors    = messages still unreadable after the retry policy below
  ceiling   = max(2, ceil(0.05 * attempted))

  errors == 0             -> note is None; nothing about holes reaches the scan
  0 < errors <= ceiling   -> the source is still OK, and returns a note naming BOTH the error count and the attempted count
  errors > ceiling        -> raise RuntimeError whose message names BOTH counts, so the source is recorded as FAILED

  Retry policy: HTTP 5xx, HTTP 429, and socket/timeout errors get EXACTLY ONE retry for that message. HTTP 4xx is counted immediately with no retry, because a 400 on an id the list endpoint just returned is a data inconsistency and a retry cannot help. Detect the status via the exception's `resp.status` attribute, which is what googleapiclient's HttpError exposes.

  Never log, print or store a message body, a subject, or a sender address as part of error handling. Failed message ids may go to stderr only.

RETURN SHAPE. Every item-producing function in intake.py must return a 3-tuple `(items, truncated, note)` where `note` is None when there is no bounded hole to declare. That means gmail_items, cal_items and cli_items all change shape, and `run()` inside `collect()` must store the note on the result dict under the key `note`. Mixed 2-tuple and 3-tuple shapes are explicitly not acceptable; the uniformity is the point, because `run()` and `write_scan` must handle every source identically. Existing callers that unpack two values must be updated. Use `results.append({... , "note": note})` and have write_scan read `r.get("note")` so a result dict written by older code cannot crash it.

SCAN RENDERING. `write_scan` (around line 379) already renders a TRUNCATED line for a source that answered with a bounded hole. Render the note the same way, immediately after that source's items and before or after the TRUNCATED line, as a line containing the word PARTIAL, both counts, and the source id in the existing `[source-id]` bracket style. A hole that exists only in the run log is invisible: the brief author reads the scan artifact, not the log.

HOW TO VERIFY, run these from /mnt/d_drive/repos/EA and iterate until both pass:
  python3 tests/test_gmail_partial.py
  python3 /tmp/claude-1000/-mnt-d-drive-repos-EA/16e106db-dbb9-44a1-936b-63218d06190f/scratchpad/check_lane_b.py

The frozen test currently reports 16 named failures. Read them; they are the specification and they name the exact expected counts. The second command is the full check the run is graded on: it re-verifies the frozen test's hash, runs the frozen test, runs every other test file in tests/ to prove you broke nothing, and asserts you touched only scripts/sources/intake.py.

STYLE. This repository's code carries dense WHY-comments explaining what incident each rule exists to prevent. Match that. Any comment you add should say what breaks if the rule is removed, not restate what the line does. Do not add dependencies. Do not restructure code beyond what the contract requires. Keep the diff small and local.

OUTPUT CONTRACT. After the checks pass, write ./notes.md in your scratch task directory containing: which functions you changed and why, the exact retry and threshold logic you implemented, how you updated every caller of the changed return shapes, the final output of both verification commands, and any assumption you had to make. If something in the contract turned out to be impossible or ambiguous, say so plainly in notes.md rather than silently choosing.
